$comment: Published structural contract for a Motion document. The AUTHORITY is the hand-written validator in packages/core/src/validate.ts (schema family 'motion'); this file encodes the document-level structural rules that validator enforces so external consumers get the same accept/reject at the structural level. It is verified against the validator by packages/core/src/motion-schema-contract.test.ts and scripts/generate-public-contracts.ts --check (required lists and the easing enum are pinned to core constants). Full-fidelity validation of every field is out of scope and remains in validate.ts; this schema is intentionally permissive (additionalProperties allowed) beyond the structural rules below.

layer.$comment: Structural layer rules enforced by validateMotionLayers in packages/core/src/validate.ts. Additional layer-shape fields (transform, style, shape, effects, mask, transitions, source, etc.) are validated by validate.ts and intentionally allowed here (additionalProperties defaults to permitted).

type.$comment: Renderable layer types (MotionLayerType, and the union of the renderer capability cards in packages/core/src/capability-cards.ts): adjustment, audio, camera, caption, environment, image, particles, scene3d, shader, shape, text, video, web. Every one of them is drawn by at least one lane; packages/core/src/layer-type-source-of-truth.test.ts fails if that stops being true, so this list is the menu of what actually works. Deliberately NOT an enum: validate.ts accepts any non-empty string type so a host can carry its own types through a document. A type outside this list is not rendered by anything — motion.package.validate refuses such a package with package_unrenderable rather than letting the first render discover it (host-produced 'html'/'canvas' layers included: the browser lane's capability gate refuses both).

keyframe.$comment: A single keyframe entry as enforced by validateKeyframe in validate.ts. `value` type depends on the keyframe target and is validated there, so it is left unconstrained here.

easing.$comment: Accepted easing forms per isSupportedEasing in packages/core/src/timeline.ts. The named enum is pinned to NAMED_EASINGS_LIST by the schema drift test; cubic-bezier(...) / steps(...) are the parametric forms.
